ops.title: Codex review passes can return stale answers from parallel sessions — verify the answer matches the question; pin scope tightly on re-runs
ops.body:
During the structured-signals migration (July 2026), two codex review passes in one session returned answers belonging to a *different* review: one refuter pass echoed the previous phase's finder findings verbatim (including items already fixed), and another codex run read back a stale `mktemp` reply file from a parallel codex session. The codex-wrapper caught the second itself by cross-checking the run log against the question text.

**Why:** parallel codex invocations in one repo can collide on scratch files/cached replies; a drifted answer looks plausible and can silently poison a review synthesis with findings about the wrong diff.

**How to apply:** when a codex answer doesn't reference the symbols/files the question named — or re-raises findings already fixed — treat it as stale, not as new signal. Re-dispatch with a single-purpose prompt that names the exact functions and the contract, and forbids findings outside that scope ("answer only about X/Y; list attacks that did NOT break"). The tightly-pinned re-runs produced excellent, substantiated traces both times. See [[named-agents-need-report-nudge]] for the adjacent delivery failure mode.
